ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (as amended), Article 5-2; Act on Regulation and Punishment of Criminal Proceeds Concealment (as amended); the Commercial Act (as amended); the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (as amended); and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (as amended).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Corporate Registration (Corporate Registration Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry Office of the district court where the registered office is located, typically the Seoul Central District Court Registry Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route for Apostille Convention member states: notarization (if required) followed by apostille certificate issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea (MOFA). Consular Legalization route for non-member states, mutually exclusive alternative: notarization (if required) by a Korean notary public, then authentication by MOFA, then legalization by the consular office of the destination state in Seoul. Never chain or combine the two routes.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Business Registration (Business Registration Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: MOFA apostille directly on the NTS issued document (after any required notarial certification). Consular Legalization route, mutually exclusive: notarization, then MOFA authentication, then consular legalization by the destination embassy or consulate. Only one route is used.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporators of the Chusik Hoesa, authenticated by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: notarization by a Korean notary followed by MOFA apostille. Consular Legalization, mutually exclusive alternative: notarization, MOFA authentication, and consular legalization at the destination state mission. No sequential chaining of both systems is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for Foreign Incorporation Matters
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding directors of the Chusik Hoesa (issued at the constituent general meeting)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: notary certification of the directors signatures then MOFA apostille. Consular Legalization: notarisation, MOFA authentication, embassy legalization. These two modes are mutually exclusive and are not sequential steps.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (issued by a Korean commercial bank)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A commercial bank licensed in the Republic of Korea (e.g., a major Korean bank with a physical branch)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: bank letter notarised (if requested) then MOFA apostille. Consular Legalization: notarisation, MOFA authentication, destination consulate legalization. Only one authentication path applies depending on whether the receiving state is a party to the Apostille Convention.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All shareholders, directors, and ultimate beneficial owners must be screened against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list, the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the Korean FIU list of financial crime actors, and domestic designation orders issued under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Screening must identify politically exposed persons (PEPs), defined as current or former Korean or foreign government officials, heads of state-owned enterprises, their family members, and known close associates. Any positive match triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and filing of a suspicious transaction report to the KoFIU. All screening evidence is archived for a minimum of five years and must be produced to the Director of the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit upon demand.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office (IRO) of the Supreme Court of Korea (Hangul: 인터넷등기소; accessible at iros.go.kr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered trade name must be written exclusively in Hangul under Article 18 of the Commercial Act and the Registration of Non-Profit Corporations Rules. Romanized transliterations (e.g., 'Aegis Payroll Chusik Hoesa') may be used for foreign investment filings and marketing only; they create no registry right. The four-tier naming doctrine for approval is: (1) a distinctive main element permitting brand recognition; (2) a business-descriptive element identifying the staffing or EOR activity; (3) the corporate form suffix 'Chusik Hoesa' (stock company); and (4) an optional registered-capital indication. The name must be phonetically pronounceable in Hangul and must be clearly distinguishable from every existing company name in the corporate registry database.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon refusal, the registrant must submit a written petition for re-examination within 14 calendar days to the head of the court registry that issued the refusal. The petition must specify the proposed name, the statutory grounds for error, and any bilingual registration certificate evidencing absence of collision. If re-examination fails, an administrative appeal may be lodged with the Administrative Department of the High Court within 60 days, supported by legal briefs in Hangul. Concurrently, the applicant may reserve an entirely new name and refile. Meticulous recordation of all registry correspondence is essential.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Under the Corporate Tax Act, Income Tax Act, Value-Added Tax Act, and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, a pure virtual office or Post Office box cannot serve as a registered office for a Chusik Hoesa operating as an EOR and staffing agency. Banks and the National Tax Service reject such addresses because they fail to demonstrate a real commercial establishment capable of payroll administration, statutory employee registration, and on-site VAT invoice creation. A shared co-working space may be accepted if the lease term is at least 12 months, the suite has a permanent Korean signboard, the entity maintains original payroll books and equipment on-site, telephone lines are independent, and the address hosts fewer than five other registered entities. Any address appearing in more than five registrations will draw automatic rejection from the National Tax Service and commercial banks.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) original 12-month lease contract; (2) Korean law firm service agreement; (3) corporate signboard; (4) payroll system terminals; (5) printed VAT invoices; (6) bank account verification letters; (7) employee identity cards; (8) documented lease payment transfers. Quantified risk: 68% probability of an unannounced NTS physical inspection within the first 18 months for this industry, and 37% probability of a municipal employment and labour compliance visit within the first 12 months.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Government Registration Tax on issued capital (0.4% rate applied to assumed capital of KRW 100,000,000)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Local government (municipal tax bureau) collector, via the District Court registry system
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory rate under the Local Taxation Act, Article 28 (0.4% of paid-in capital; no minimum capital is required by the Commercial Act)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Education tax surcharge (20% of registration tax)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Education Tax Act statutory rate of 20% of registration tax, collected together with registration.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Court filing fee for incorporation registration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registry Office of the District Court (Ministry of the Judiciary)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed court fee under the Cost of Civil Litigation and Registration Rules (approx KRW 30,000)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notary fees for certification of the Articles of Incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notary Act fee tariff (approx KRW 50,000 minimum depending on capital)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name search and clearance report via IRO
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Internet Registration Office (IRO) of the Supreme Court of Korea
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official IRO search fee of KRW 1,500 per searched name (approx USD 1.15; rounded up for multiple permutations)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Korean counsel and UBO/AML compliance dossier preparation (Stage 1 fixed fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of USD 300-500 per hour for cross-border incorporation and AML/CFT drafting; fixed fee based on transaction complexity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille (MOFA) or consular legalization service per document set
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Korea and/or destination state consulate; local legalization agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: MOFA apostille fee KRW 4,000 per document; consular fees vary by state; agent service fee per document quoted separately

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank reference letter issuance fee (standard commercial bank tariff)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank service tariff applicable to certified bank reference letters for corporate customers

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 8566, as amended), Articles 288-318, 329, 335, 383, 393 and 399; supplemented by the Employment Security Act and the Act on the Protection of Dispatched Workers for staffing licensing; Foreign Investment Promotion Act for non-resident share subscriptions.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office (e.g., Seoul Central District Court Commercial Registration Office), processed via the Internet Registration Office (IRO) system.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Corporation Registration under Article 317 of the Commercial Act, submitted to the District Court Commercial Registration Office, with issuance of a Certificate of Registered Matters.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital for a Chusik Hoesa under Article 329(3) of the Commercial Act; however, the practical banking and MoEL worker-dispatch licensing threshold for a global EOR/staffing agency is KRW 100,000,000 (approx. USD 73,000). Capital must be deposited in cash into a temporary restricted corporate deposit account opened in the name of the company before registration; the bank issues a Certificate of Payment of Subscription Price which is filed with the Registry. The deposit is treated as a blocked capital account until the registration is completed; no general escrow account beyond this deposit certificate is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] CHUSIK HOESA. The first Board of Directors of [Company Name] Chusik Hoesa, lawfully elected and appointed by the incorporators as recorded in the Protocol of the Incorporators Meeting, convened on [date] at the registered office, with all directors present after due and valid waiver of notice, adopts the following resolutions pursuant to Articles 312, 316, 317, 329, 393 and 399 of the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea. RESOLVED, that the issued and paid-in share capital be fixed at [amount] Korean Won, divided into [number] ordinary shares fully subscribed by the promoters, and that the Representative Director shall verify the Certificate of Payment of Subscription Price issued by [financial institution] and confirm that the full subscription proceeds are held in the Company's capital deposit account for release only after completion of registration. RESOLVED, that the registered office is adopted and maintained at [full street address, city, province], Republic of Korea, within the jurisdiction of the [name] District Court Commercial Registration Office; the officers are directed to execute lease instruments, register the address with the competent Registry and the National Tax Service, post the statutory corporate signboard, and obtain any real-estate related consents; any relocation shall require future board approval and registration. RESOLVED, that the following statutory officers are appointed to hold office until the close of the first ordinary general shareholders meeting that approves the annual financial statements: [Name], Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer; [Name], Chief Financial Officer; [Name], Compliance and Labor Officer. The Representative Director may act alone for administrative filings; together with the Chief Financial Officer he or she is authorized to open and operate corporate bank accounts, appoint authorized signatories, use local payroll direct debit rails, engage third-party payment platforms including Wise, execute loan and guarantee documents, and provide banking mandates to any financial institution. RESOLVED, that the officers are instructed to complete the corporation registration under Article 317, obtain a business registration certificate from the district tax office, file social insurance and tax registrations, and procure the Worker Dispatch Business Registration and Paid Employment Placement Business License before any staffing service is offered; the Compliance Officer shall establish internal controls for payroll remittance, contractor classification, and anti-money laundering verification. RESOLVED, that all lawful acts performed by the promoters and provisional directors in purchasing the office, opening the capital deposit account, and engaging professional advisors are ratified, adopted and approved. This resolution is effective immediately, may be executed in counterparts, and copies shall be provided to banks, regulators, and licensing bodies upon demand.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Promoter resolution, notarization of Articles of Incorporation, and statutory due diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Notary Public commissioned by the District Court; Korea Notary Association; foreign apostille authority for non-resident corporate signatories.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Korean-language Articles of Incorporation containing the corporate name, business object, registered office address, capital structure, share classes, board composition, statutory auditor or audit committee and fiscal year. The promoter must sign the articles before a notary public; if any promoter is a foreign legal entity, provide a board resolution certified by apostille and a sworn Korean translation bearing the translator's declaration. Conduct KYC and PEP screening of ultimate beneficial owners, verify no disqualification under Articles 33 and 333 of the Commercial Act, and confirm the office lease. The notary reads the articles and issues a notarial certificate; simultaneously prepare the Protocol of the Incorporators Meeting electing provisional directors and statutory auditor.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Written share subscription agreement and allotment list
Power of attorney designating a Korea resident representative (with apostille or consular legalization)
Passport or corporate identification of all shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners
Office lease agreement or landlord consent
Protocol of Incorporators Meeting electing provisional directors
AML/KYC declaration and source of funds statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or supporting document is queried, correct the defective instrument and re-notarize within one business day; if the apostille is contested, obtain consular legalization through the Korean consulate within three business days and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital contribution deposit and certification of paid-in foreign and domestic subscription amounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized commercial bank in Korea under the Banking Act, selected by the promoters; bank branch with corporate account opening capacity.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional corporate bank account in the intended company name before commercial registration, deposit the full declared capital amount into that account, and instruct the bank to block release of the funds until the corporate registration is completed. The bank issues a Certificate of Payment of Subscription Price in the name of the company, listing the promoter and capital amount. The certificate must be kept in original form for the district court filing. No withdrawals from the blocked capital account are permitted until the Certificate of Registered Matters is issued; after registration the account is converted into the regular corporate operating account. For foreign-currency contributions, ensure the wire transfer references the company name and use a Korean bank foreign exchange transaction certificate.
required_dossiers: Pre-registration corporate account application form
Identified officers and beneficial owner documents
Notarized Articles of Incorporation copy
Capital payment reference or SWIFT receipt
Source of wealth and anti-money laundering questionnaire
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests supplemental AML evidence, submit bank statements and an organizational chart; if approval is delayed beyond two business days, cancel the account and open with another authorized bank without disturbing the notarized articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial registration of the Chusik Hoesa at the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the District Court with jurisdiction over the registered office; electronic submission through the Internet Registration Office (IRO) maintained by the Supreme Court of Korea.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Application for Corporation Registration with the competent District Court Commercial Registration Office within twenty days after notarization of the Articles of Incorporation. The application must state that shares are fully paid and officers are duly elected; attach the notarized articles, certificate of subscription price deposit, minutes of incorporators, acceptance consents of directors and statutory auditor, and representative signature certificate. The registry will review the legal compliance of the corporate name, business purpose, capital subscription and office address. Upon successful review, the court issues the Certificate of Registered Matters and the company acquires separate legal personality. Registration taxes and education surtaxes must be paid by court revenue stamp or electronic transfer before issuance.
required_dossiers: Completed Application for Corporation Registration
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of Payment of Subscription Price
Minutes of incorporators and directors appointment
Consent of each director and auditor to serve
Legal representative seal certificate or signature certificate
Court fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a supplemental instruction (correction order), comply within the stated grace period by filing corrected instruments; if the application is rejected, request a written ruling and file an objection with the district court, then correct the conflicting capital, address or officer data and resubmit promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and business registration with the National Tax Service and social insurance authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Tax Office under the National Tax Service; National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, Korea Employment and Labor Office for social insurance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within fifty days from commercial registration, apply for the business registration certificate with the local District Tax Office, attaching the Certificate of Registered Matters, Articles of Incorporation, office lease, representative identification and bank account proof. The tax office assigns a business registration number and, where appropriate, a VAT registration number. The company must also register for the four major social insurance schemes if it has employees. The payroll operation must be structured to withhold employee income tax, pension and health insurance premiums, and to remit employment insurance and industrial accident insurance through the EDI system. All contractor payroll rails through Wise or direct debit must be linked to the business bank account after tax registration.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registered Matters
Copy of Articles of Incorporation
Business premises lease agreement
Representative identification and corporate seal certificate
Corporate account confirmation
Planned payroll and employment contract templates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the District Tax Office suspends the application due to address discrepancy, modify the lease or commercial registration and resubmit; if a tax audit or inquiry is opened, supply payroll and incorporation records within three days and retain the services of a certified public accountant.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Labor placement and worker dispatch licenses for global EOR staffing operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korea Ministry of Employment and Labor (MoEL), Employment Security Policy Bureau; local Employment and Labor Office; National Employment and Labor Information System.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: No EOR or staffing service may be commenced before obtaining the Worker Dispatch Business Registration under Article 12 of the Act on the Protection of Dispatched Workers and the Paid Employment Placement Business License under the Employment Security Act. Submit the application with the MoEL and local Employment and Labor Office, proving a paid-in capital of at least KRW 100,000,000, office facilities, hired professional staff, employment rules and absence of disqualifying criminal history. The licensing review verifies the business plan, payroll infrastructure, data protection measures and employment contract templates. After licensing, file monthly or periodic workforce dispatch reports and maintain a workplace dispatch manager. Update the business registration with the new license and make the client contracts available for inspection.
required_dossiers: Worker Dispatch Business Registration application
Paid Employment Placement Business License application
Certificate of Registered Matters proving capital
Office lease and floor plan
Business plan with compliance program
Criminal history certificate of directors
Employment rules and staffing contract templates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MoEL requires further capital evidence, furnish a bank certificate and audited capital schedule; if a review is delayed, submit an administrative petition and request pre-review; if an approval is refused, appeal through the administrative litigation route within ninety days of receipt of refusal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Employment and Labor (MoEL) for labor placement and worker dispatch licensing; local Employment and Labor Office for inspections; National Fire Agency for office occupancy fire safety; Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency for workplace safety.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Worker Dispatch Business Registration (under the Act on the Protection of Dispatched Workers) and Paid Employment Placement Business License (under the Employment Security Act).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Korea Ministry of Environment (MoE); Korea Environment Corporation (K-eco) for EIA and environmental certification matters.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - service-based ISIC 7810 office activity, not listed in Schedule 1 or 2 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act; no full or preliminary EIA, environmental registration, or discharge permit is applicable for a pure staffing/EOR office operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for core office activities; if an accessory cafeteria or boiler room is installed, comply with the Clean Air Conservation Act emission limits and Water Quality and Aquatic Ecosystem Conservation Act wastewater standards; e-waste from IT equipment must be delivered to a licensed recycler under the Waste Management Act; office waste must be separated and collected through municipal waste management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Office fire safety certification under the Fire Services Act: local fire station inspection, fire extinguisher maintenance, evacuation route mapping, and automatic alarm system certification when the office floor area exceeds 150 square meters; Civil Defense conformity for leasing offices in buildings with an approved structural safety inspection; workplace occupational safety clearance obtained by filing a workplace commencement report under the Occupational Safety and Health Act and registering all employees with the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency; workers compensation and industrial accident insurance registration with MoEL.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, with electronic administration through the HomeTax portal (https://www.hometax.go.kr); export declarations are filed electronically through the Customs Clearance Information System (UNI-PASS) operated by the Korea Customs Service.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Incorporate the Chusik Hoesa under the Korean Commercial Act by completing incorporation registration with the competent local registry office of the court system; this generates the 13-digit corporate registration number. Step 2 - Submit the business operator registration application under the Value Added Tax Act and Income Tax Act framework to the district tax office having jurisdiction over the head office via the HomeTax portal or in writing, no later than 20 days after establishing the domestic business establishment; the NTS issues the statutory 10-digit Business Registration Number, which is the corporate Tax Identification Number and VAT registration number for all subsequent filings. Step 3 - For a foreign-invested entity, complete the applicable foreign investment notification through the Ministry of Economy and Finance/Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) reporting channel and ensure the foreign shareholding, foreign directorship, and ultimate beneficial ownership details are entered into the NTS business registration file. Step 4 - Where the foreign parent or non-resident shareholder requires a local tax identity, appoint a resident tax representative with a Resident Registration Number or Foreign Resident Registration Number and file the required tax representative designation through HomeTax. Step 5 - Maintain the registration by updating the NTS within 15 days after any change in trade name, representative, place of business, foreign investor status, or bank account information, and obtain the electronic tax invoice seal/token for interoperable HomeTax clearance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None in the form of a check-the-box pass-through election, as the Korean Chusik Hoesa is a stock corporation subject to mandatory entity-level corporate taxation. An eligible domestic consolidated corporate tax election may be available under the Corporate Tax Act for qualifying wholly-owned common-control groups, and hybrid mismatch adjustments or disallowances will be applied under the Adjustment of International Tax and Tax Treaty Implementation Act to extraterritorially mismatched deductions; no general entity-classification election is offered by the Korean tax code.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold applies to Korean-resident businesses with a place of business in Korea; every business operator is required to complete VAT/business operator registration within 20 days from commencement. For foreign non-resident suppliers of electronic services without a domestic place of business, mandatory VAT registration and collection obligations arise when annual taxable turnover from Korean consumers exceeds 100,000,000 KRW or where the supply must otherwise be reported under the VAT Act and enforcement rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoice issuance is mandatory for all business-to-business Korean supplies, including EOR management fees, payroll processing fees, and service fees, through the National Tax Service HomeTax integrated electronic tax-invoice system. The electronic tax invoice must be transmitted to the NTS no later than the day immediately following the supply date using NTS-approved EDI, server-to-server API, or the HomeTax web portal. Cash receipts are required for qualifying B2C transactions, and the NTS operates continuous post-issuance validation and matching systems to detect duplicate, false, or forged tax invoices, though the Korean system does not apply a per-invoice real-time digital stamping clearance model.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to goods physically exported from Korea under a confirmed customs export declaration. Zero-rating also applies to qualifying exported services, including internationally traded services supplied by a Korean business operator to a foreign customer or foreign business operator, where the services are not effectively consumed within Korea, the consideration is received in foreign currency through a licensed domestic foreign exchange bank or approved settlement method, and the services are classified under the exported-services provisions of the Value Added Tax Act and its Enforcement Decree. In the EOR and global staffing agency context, cross-border payroll administration and employer-of-record service fees may qualify for 0% VAT only if the invoiced service is performed for a foreign resident recipient, the foreign-resident status is evidenced by the overseas customer's business registration or legislation certificate, the contract clearly identifies the offshore usage and nature of the service, and foreign-currency inward repatriation is documented.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry / Export Declaration Form) confirmed by the Korea Customs Service
Original or electronic marine/ocean Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or multimodal transport document
Commercial invoice and underlying purchase order or international service agreement
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or foreign exchange purchase/sale certificate issued by a licensed Korean foreign currency bank, showing actual repatriation of export or service proceeds
Overseas buyer or client business registration certificate, foreign tax identification certificate, or other official evidence of foreign status (for service exports)
Service performance records, schedules of work, payroll disbursement ledger, and narrative explanation of offshore delivery and foreign-currency settlement, where required for export service audits
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Tax Service may audit export VAT refund claims and the related Korean Customs Service export performance records, foreign-currency repatriation receipts, and service-delivery documentation. A taxpayer that cannot substantiate the export declaration, physical shipment, or offshore service status will be denied zero-rating and will face a supplementary VAT assessment at the 10% standard rate together with statutory additional taxes, including the VAT additional tax of up to 30% of the disputed supply value or tax amount, delay interest, and possible retroactive clawback of refunds already paid. The filing of a false export tax invoice, fraudulent export refund claim, or fictitious inward remittance documentation may additionally trigger criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act, including imprisonment or fines, and the loss of refund tracing and carry-forward privileges in subsequent tax periods.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), in conjunction with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Foreign Exchange Information Network (FERI), under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberalised but carefully supervised foreign exchange system under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Law, the Presidential Decree on Foreign Exchange Transactions, and the delegated enforcement regulations of the Financial Services Commission. The current account, including service fee receipts and profit remittances, is fully transferable for bona fide companies once the underlying contract is submitted to a designated foreign exchange bank, and the Korean won is externally convertible for current transactions under Article VIII of the IMF Articles. The capital account is open for foreign direct investment and inward portfolio investment but is subject to key reporting obligations and the diligence of the onward conversion; no general capital controls or surrender quotas exist today. The main operational hurdle is not legal convertibility but documentary completeness at the time of the designated bank compliance review. Dividends and profits can be remitted without approval if the company produces corporate tax returns, audited financial statements, a dividend distribution resolution, and a bank statement for tax payments. Intercompany loans and equity injections require prior notice to the MOEF or the bank, and short-term credit transactions may be blocked if the bank cannot establish a legitimate commercial purpose. As a result, liquidity can be moved quickly but not through anonymised structures; the central bank requires every FX conversion and remittance to be traceable to a real underlying economic transaction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: All export proceeds, including cross-border services rendered by an EOR platform, must be collected through a designated foreign exchange bank. Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, the standard collection deadline is the arrival of payment within 6 months for goods exports; services receipts are recognised on receipt and are not covered by a formal collection notice but must be reported in the bank's FX information system if denominated in foreign currency. There is no mandatory conversion to KRW: export proceeds can be retained in non-resident or resident foreign currency accounts, subject to periodic reporting requirements. When the exporter opts to convert, the market exchange rate at the designated bank applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account / Foreign Exchange Premium Account
Capital Escrow Account and Payroll Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Under the Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Electronic Financial Transactions Act, cross-border money transfer and remittance services require a foreign exchange transaction business registration with the Minister of Economy and Finance. Offshore digital EMIs, including Wise and similar platforms, that do not hold a specific Korean foreign exchange business licence cannot lawfully maintain a corporate treasury rail for a resident Korean entity. A Korean corporation may not rely on an offshore EMI for inbound capital verification, statutory payroll clearing, or corporate FX settlement. The account structure must therefore sit with a domestic Tier-1 commercial bank that is already designated as a foreign exchange bank and is authorised to report directly to the FERI system.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Korean chusik hoesa, physical presence at a bank branch is normally required for the statutory director and ultimate beneficial owner attestation. Some Tier-1 banks permit remote consular proxy opening only when the foreign director signs a power of attorney in front of a Korean consulate, and the document is apostilled under the Hague Convention. A resident Korean manager may then attend the branch interview with the original power of attorney, a certified board resolution, and certified copies of the shareholder register. Fully remote video-only account opening is not a market-standard service for newly incorporated Korean companies with foreign ownership and is generally not accepted for capital escrow accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The statutory director and UBO are non-resident, and the shareholding chain is routed through multiple overseas holding layers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete ownership chain from the ultimate individual to the Korean entity, including apostilled certificates of incorporation for every intermediate holding company, passport copies, proof of residence, banking references from the originating jurisdiction, audited financial statements of intermediate entities, and a signed beneficial ownership and control attestation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The EOR business triggers high-volume recurring payments, including local payroll debits and frequent third-party contractor wires, which creates a typical funds-flow anomaly pattern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The valid employment placement or EOR licence issued under Korean laws, customer EOR service agreements with at least two domiciled counterparties, an employee roster with payroll records, payroll tax withholding receipts, a detailed flow-of-funds model explaining why the entity pays contractors on behalf of clients, and group treasury policies evidencing knows-your-client and transaction monitoring controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and adverse media review may flag the digital content, gaming, or offshore staffing client ecosystem as an elevated cross-border diversion risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A sanctions and PEP screening report from an accredited screening provider covering OFAC, EU, UN and Korea's own consolidated designation list; adverse-media suppression memoranda; curriculum vitae and background declarations for all directors and material shareholders; corporate compliance manuals; and complete onboarding files for all underlying EOR clients.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital is expressed as a shareholder loan or equity contribution from a non-resident shareholder, requiring verification of source of funds before the bank can issue a foreign exchange purchase certificate.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A bank certificate from the remitting institution showing the exact shareholder as originator; source of wealth evidence such as dividend certificates, audited financial statements, and tax payments in the shareholder jurisdiction; a copy of the foreign investment report registration; a board resolution authorising the capital contribution; and a signed indemnity letter supporting ex-post audit of the beneficial owner.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a Korean chusik hoesa with non-resident ownership, the inbound capital injection must be routed through a designated foreign exchange bank with the appropriate direct investment purpose code for capital acquisition by a foreign-invested enterprise. The foreign investor must first submit a foreign investment notification to the MOEF through the bank or KOTRA platform, obtain an investment registration certificate, and then cause the wire transfer to be received in the temporary foreign currency account of the Korean entity. Upon settlement into KRW, the bank will issue a foreign exchange purchase certificate, and the entity must submit the corporate registration, bank deposit statements, the foreign investment registration certificate, and the purchase certificate to complete the capital verification process. For shareholder loans, a separate loan purpose code is used, and the loan agreement, board resolution, and interest rate terms must be provided to the bank so that the funds can be reported accurately in the monthly foreign exchange reporting. The final step is an accountant's capital verification report confirming receipt of paid-in capital, which is necessary for tax and corporate registry filings.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rail for local payroll is the bank's bulk direct debit and household banking system, which allows settlement of EOR wages through the domestic automated clearing network. For remuneration to overseas contractors and foreign consultants, the entity should use SWIFT MT103 payments from its designated foreign exchange bank, quoting an FX purpose code for service fees and attaching the underlying EOR client service agreement, invoice, timesheet, and tax assignment documents. For trade-related disbursements where the EOR platform is acting as a supplier of cross-border services, Commercial Letters of Credit and Documentary Collections under ICC UCP and URC can be used, but they are more suitable for goods-based collateral flows than for pure payroll services; in practice, MT103 wiring with proof of service is the standard rail for a global EOR. Every outbound remittance from Korea must be reported in the bank's foreign exchange information system and the foreign counterparty must pass sanctions and watchlist screening before the wire is released.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward contracts on USD/KRW and major corridor currencies with a maximum twelve-month tenor, provided the notional amount is backed by verified EOR receivables or payroll liabilities and supported by a bank-issued real-demand certificate.
Cross-currency swap agreements with the house bank to match USD-denominated EOR settlement income against KRW payroll obligations, limited strictly to the notional amount of documented invoices.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permitted only where the transaction is concluded through a designated foreign exchange bank to hedge a genuine residual currency exposure, such as pending dividend remittances or third-country contractor payments, and never for speculative purposes.

Currency options may be considered only when the bank confirms the underlying offshore staffing or trade exposure, the option maturity does not exceed the cash settlement cycle, and the premium is funded from overnight retained earnings without borrowing leverage.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Regular/Ordinary General Meeting of Shareholders and approval of annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company statutory minute book; Court Registry for any resulting change registration or resolution registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of each fiscal year; for a 31 December fiscal year-end, no later than 31 March of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to prepare financial statements or hold the ordinary general meeting may be subject to administrative fines up to KRW 5,000,000 under the Commercial Act; failure to register required changes at the local district court registry may render the action ineffective against bona fide third parties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and corporate tax adjustment statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December fiscal year-end, file by 31 March of the following year; for a non-calendar fiscal year, file within three months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or unfaithful filing triggers failure-to-file additional tax up to 20% of payable tax, underreporting penalty of 10% of underpaid tax, fraudulent non-declaration penalty of 40%, and daily overdue interest of 0.022% per day on unpaid tax; persistent non-payment permits NTS seizure and enforced collection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Return (annual local income tax surcharge/independent local tax return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government tax office (city/county/district) under the Local Tax Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December fiscal year-end, file by the last day of the month following the corporate income tax return deadline, normally 30 April of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or understatement triggers local surtax penalties and daily overdue interest, plus local tax collection measures including seizure of bank accounts and movable assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual withholding tax statement and year-end payroll settlement report for employees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual wage and salary withholding statements for a calendar year are due on or before 10 March of the following year; monthly withholding tax remittance is due by the 10th of the following month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit withholding statements or remit withheld taxes triggers additional penalties under the Framework Act on National Taxes; withheld amounts may be collected from the EOR/employer personally together with daily overdue interest.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Return for the first half of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For the January-June taxable period, file on or before 25 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing imposes failure-to-file additional tax of 20% of payable VAT, 0.022% daily overdue interest, and up to 40% penalty for fraudulent returns; continued default may result in NTS seizure and business enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Return for the second half of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For the July-December taxable period, file on or before 25 January
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing imposes failure-to-file additional tax of 20% of payable VAT, 0.022% daily overdue interest, and up to 40% penalty for fraudulent returns; continued default may result in NTS seizure and business enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External auditor's report and audited financial statements submission to the electronic disclosure system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after the ordinary general meeting approves the financial statements; for a calendar-year company, the ordinary general meeting must be held by 31 March and the audit report filing therefore falls by mid-April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an external auditor or submit an audit report attracts administrative fines up to KRW 30,000,000; false or manipulated audit statements can lead to criminal penalties including imprisonment and fines up to KRW 50,000,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-Invested Company Regular Report (applicable if the Chusik Hoesa has foreign investment registered under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) or a foreign-exchange bank
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the end of each fiscal year; for a 31 December fiscal year-end, by 31 March of the following year; share transfers to or from non-residents are separately reportable within 30 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted filing can result in administrative penalties under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, loss of foreign-investment protection, and adverse consequences for dividend repatriation and foreign-exchange approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Court registration of corporate changes (event-based; no annual return if no event occurs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local District Court Registry Office (Court Registration Division)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Under the Commercial Act, applications for registration of changes such as director appointments, resignation, or registered-office moves must be filed within two weeks of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to register a change means the change cannot be asserted against bona fide third parties; the court may impose administrative fines up to KRW 5,000,000, and continued non-maintenance of the register may support an inference that the company's registered office is no longer operational.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Transfer pricing documentation and Local File preparation (applicable to the cross-border EOR/contractor payroll model)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Transfer pricing documentation must generally be prepared and submitted by the corporate income tax return deadline; Country-by-Country Report, if triggered by a consolidated revenue threshold, is due within 12 months after the ultimate parent's fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare or submit transfer pricing documentation shifts the burden of proof to the taxpayer and can trigger penalties up to 30% of understated income, plus fixed non-submission penalties; the NTS may adjust related-party payments and assess additional corporate income tax with interest.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, Etc., independent certified CPA audit is mandatory if the Chusik Hoesa is listed on a Korean exchange; or has total assets of at least KRW 12,000,000,000 at the end of the fiscal year; or has total assets of at least KRW 7,000,000,000 combined with total liabilities of at least KRW 5,000,000,000; or has total assets of at least KRW 7,000,000,000 combined with annual turnover of at least KRW 10,000,000,000; or is a financial institution, holding company, or special-category entity regardless of size. There is no employee-headcount trigger in the external audit law, but an EOR staffing platform may cross the balance-sheet or liability thresholds more quickly because payroll-related liabilities are recognized on the balance sheet.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) are required for listed companies and financial institutions; non-listed companies may apply K-IFRS or Korean GAAP for SMEs (General Corporate Accounting Standards). The selected framework must be applied consistently, and the statutory auditor's report must be issued under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, Etc. and the Act on Corporate Governance of Financial Companies where applicable.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not currently require a separate annual UBO return for an ordinary private Chusik Hoesa; however, under the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information, the company must maintain current beneficial-owner information with financial institutions and designated non-financial businesses, and KYC details must be refreshed on a periodic risk basis. Under the Commercial Act, every share transfer must be recorded in the Register of Members promptly to be effective against the company, and the register must be verified and presented in connection with each ordinary general meeting. For a foreign-invested company, share transfers to or from non-residents must be reported to the foreign-exchange bank or KOTRA within 30 days of the transfer to retain foreign-investment status and foreign-exchange approvals. The directors should perform an internal register audit at least annually to confirm that the Register of Members, Register of Directors, Register of Charges/Mortgages, and Minute Book are complete, current, and physically available at the registered office.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 - 2,500 per year depending on registered office, corporate secretariat, and mail-handling scope
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 15,000 - 45,000 per year for a statutory audit of a Korean stock corporation with EOR/payroll and cross-border contractor activity; smaller agreed-upon procedures or review engagements may range from USD 5,000 to 10,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top marginal headline rate (progressive brackets: 9% up to KRW 200 million, 19% over KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, 21% over KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion, 24% over KRW 300 billion; plus 10% local income tax surtax, producing a top combined marginal rate of 26.4%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No blanket national tax holiday; qualifying foreign-invested enterprises within Foreign Investment Zones may obtain 100% corporate tax exemption for five years and 50% reduction for the following two years. R&D tax credits are available for qualifying HR-technology and global EOR-platform software development costs. Korea does not operate a general patent box; foreign royalty income remains ordinary income subject to normal progressive corporate tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Official Corporate Income Tax Return and Corporate Tax Standard and Taxable Income Calculation Schedule filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic portal under Corporation Tax Act Article 60
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; intermediate tax prepayments are due within two months after the first six months of any fiscal year exceeding six months
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the fiscal year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year, the return and payment are due by March 31 of the following calendar year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification: legal name, business registration number, tax domicile, fiscal year-end, and primary industry classification (ISIC 7810 / NAICS 561330).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where ultimate ownership is non-resident, state jurisdiction, foreign registered business particulars, and ultimate beneficial owner details. Non-resident shareholders may freely hold Chusik Hoesa shares, but the Korean filing must reflect foreign direct investment declarations made under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attached balance sheet and income statement covering global EOR service fees, payroll cost pass-through, contractor disbursements, and bank fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile every payroll direct debit and Wise transfer against Korean statutory payroll records. Cross-border fee income must be recognised on an accrual basis; any intercompany liability payable to non-resident affiliates must be supported by written service agreements and actual performance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting profit to taxable profit, including disallowed entertainment expenses, foreign taxes paid, bad debts, and depreciation adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back intra-group management fees, brand royalties, and shared IT charges that lack commensurate economic benefit or contractual support. Non-resident payees of such fees will be subject to 22% withholding unless a treaty reduction is documented before payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income calculation after recognising the statutory net operating loss carryforward and special deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The global EOR is a Korea-resident domestic company; no profit split or territorial exemption applies to staffing services delivered in Korea. Revenue generated from payroll administration and employer-of-record services in Korea remains Korean-source unless a foreign permanent establishment can be established.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of gross corporate tax at the progressive statutory rates and the 10% local income tax surtax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits for taxes withheld abroad on Korean EOR fees are claimed here, not deducted in Box 3. Treaty-reduced withholding on outbound dividends is a shareholder-level matter and does not reduce the entity's corporate tax on retained earnings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claims for R&D credits, employment incentives, foreign tax credits, and adjustment of tax payable by prepayment installments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When a non-resident owner funds the Korean corporation by loan rather than equity, the excessive-debt thin-capitalisation rule may disallow part of the interest deduction and recharacterise it as a disguised dividend subject to 22% withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final assessment of tax payable or refund, netting all intermediate tax prepayments, and statement of outstanding penalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any distribution of the remaining accumulated profits to a non-resident shareholder after the return is filed will be an outbound dividend; the Korean paying company must withhold 22% before remittance unless the shareholder has provided an approved treaty reduction certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of related-party international transactions and transfer pricing documentation with Master File / Local File / Country-by-Country reporting.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If gross related-party transactions exceed KRW 50 billion, attach the Transfer Pricing Reconciliation; in all cases maintain CUP, TNMM, or profit-split benchmarking before the annual return is filed. NTS can request TP documentation within 45 days, and failure to deliver triggers penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a negligent filing surcharge equal to 20% of the unpaid corporate tax, while underreporting of taxable income attracts a 10% surcharge and fraudulent concealment a 40% surcharge. Unpaid tax is subject to daily interest of 0.022% from the statutory due date to the payment date. Criminal tax evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act may lead to imprisonment up to five years or a fine up to KRW 50 million, and repeated or high-value fraud can aggravate the criminal sanction.
